purpose: Every asset spec in the design system says "one claim, twelve words or fewer" and then leaves the producer to invent one. This is the file that stops that. A claim on a thumbnail is brand voice at its most compressed and least reviewed, so it gets a bank, a version and a changelog like everything else.

rules.use: Pick from the bank. A new claim is a CR, not a production decision.
rules.gate: Every claim passes the Codex: no em dashes, UK English, frustration at systems never people, no vendor numbers, "gets the call" never "paged".
rules.length: Twelve words maximum. Under eight is better. A claim that needs a comma is usually two claims.
rules.repetition: A claim may be reused across surfaces but not twice in the same week on the same channel. The bank is large enough that it does not need to be.
rules.pairing: A claim carries one hinge. If the asset needs two ideas, it is the wrong asset.
rules.retire: A claim that has run four times moves to resting for a quarter. Overuse is how a line becomes a slogan, and a slogan is the opposite of a practitioner talking.

claims.text: It was never the tooling.
claims.hinge: The tool was fine. The organisation around it was not.

claims.text: Own the signal. Rent the platform.
claims.hinge: Vendors are replaceable. Your instrumentation and your ownership model are not.

claims.text: Cost is a design decision.
claims.hinge: Cardinality, retention and sampling were chosen, not inherited.

claims.text: Retention is a bet, not a setting.
claims.hinge: Thirteen months of everything is a wager nobody wrote down.

claims.text: Nobody owns the outcome.
claims.hinge: Three teams own a piece each, so the answer belongs to no one.

claims.text: Spend went up. Outcomes went down.
claims.hinge: The evidence slide. Always paired with a named, dated source.
claims.note: Never runs without the source named on the same surface.

claims.text: A leadership problem wearing a tooling costume.
claims.hinge: The reorganisation you are avoiding is the fix you are shopping for.

claims.text: Forty minutes to agree who is on the call.
claims.hinge: The bridge call is the audit. It shows you exactly what you built.

claims.text: Your dashboard is not your strategy.
claims.hinge: Twelve panels is not a plan. It is twelve deferred decisions.

claims.text: The alert fired. Nobody moved.
claims.hinge: Detection was never the bottleneck. Ownership was.

claims.text: Chosen by accident. Defended for two years.
claims.hinge: The cardinality decision nobody remembers making and everybody now protects.

claims.text: You cannot buy a culture of ownership.
claims.hinge: No procurement cycle produces the thing you actually need.

claims.text: Instrument the journey, not the box.
claims.hinge: Host metrics tell you the server is fine while the customer cannot check out.

claims.text: Every dashboard is a decision someone stopped making.
claims.hinge: Automation of a judgement is not the same as making it.

claims.text: More signal will not tell you who answers.
claims.hinge: The gap is human, so more telemetry cannot close it.

claims.text: The team that will not go first.
claims.hinge: Migration stalls on the one group with the most to lose and the least to gain.

claims.text: Observability is a question you can answer.
claims.hinge: Not a product category. A capability, tested by whether you get an answer.

claims.text: Who gets the call at three in the morning?
claims.hinge: Every architecture decision eventually becomes somebody’s night.

claims.text: The platform was fine. The boundaries were not.
claims.hinge: Ownership boundaries, not technology, decide recovery time.

claims.text: Decide retention on purpose, in writing.
claims.hinge: The forward close. One action, specific, doable on Monday.

claims.text: Rendering is not shipping.
claims.hinge: Internal discipline claim. Use only where the audience is practitioners.
claims.note: Reads as process-nerd inside the audience and as jargon outside it. Channel-limited on purpose.

claims.text: Observability that survives the bridge call.
claims.hinge: The positioning line. The test is the worst hour, not the demo.

changelog.change: Bank created. Twenty-two claims lifted from shipped posts, the advisory page, the deck masters and the book, so every line has already survived a Codex pass in context. Nothing here is newly invented copy.
